newsitem.title: GERMANY: Depfa to ask for more authorised capital.
newsitem.headline: Depfa to ask for more authorised capital.

text.p: WIESBADEN, Germany, May 14 (Reuter )- Germany's Deutsche Pfandbrief- und Hypothekenbank AG said on Wednesday it would ask shareholders to approve the creation of authorised capital at its next shareholder meeting with the aim of financing possible future acquisitions.

"Targeted acquisitions can substantially increase the earnings potential and return on equity of our group," chief executive Thilo Koepfler said in the text of a speech distributed before a news conference.
"That is why our board has taken the decision to ask the annual shareholder meeting to create authorised and conditional capital," Koepfler said.
The shareholder meeting is on June 25.
Koepfler said that Depfa did not need to raise capital for its regular operating business which was sufficiently capitalised.
"We belong to the fairly small circle of German banks which can finance their core capital from their own earnings," Koepfler said.
The banks plans to create 25 million marks of authorised capital to be used by June 25, 2002.
The bank is also seeking approval to issue up to 300 million marks worth of convertible and warrant bonds.
Depfa is a leading issuer of Pfandbrief mortgage bonds.
